newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes down, Brent/Dubai pulls WAf to Asia.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes down, Brent/Dubai pulls WAf to Asia.

text.p: Asian heavy sweet crude prices firmed slightly Wednesday, as the June overhang disappears.
But the narrow Brent/Dubai spread has created healthy Asian buying for Brent-related crudes from West Africa and Yemen.
A July loading cargo each of Qua Iboe and Zafiru were sold to South Korea by a major, although price details were unclear.
This followed a Djeno/Palanca trade also heard sold to South Korea by a Euro major.
Falls in the Brent price this week had narrowed the Brent/Dubai differential to 55/65 cents per barrel, compared to 80/95 early last week.
Traders said they expected more West African cargoes to move into Asia, citing good demand from South Korean and China.
But these cargoes would only arrive in August, giving Asian crude sellers lead time in disposing of July regional crudes.
A shosha heard sold a June parcel of Minas to China early this week at ICP -8 cents per barrel, firmer than a June Minas purchased last week by a Japanese refiner at ICP -20.
Those were probably the last June Minas barrels, traders said.
The July Minas market would become active only after the release of Indonesia's monthly allocations, due out next week.
The Middle East crude market was quiet, with just a few cargoes of Oman and Abu Dhabi cargoes available for July.
But Masila was firm, with most of the July supplies committed.
The latest Masila trade heard was an end July cargo sold to a Japanese refiner at whole month OSP +28.
Masila trades are usually priced on a five-day OSP around the bill of lading and the seller had earlier bought the cargo at OSP +13, traders said.
But with Brent in contango, the difference in premium would be minimal, they said.
